layer_note: The close of Konganar's Vaalai Kummi and an appended five-stanza kummi. The social layer is plain and high-confidence throughout (false gurus, pilgrimage turned inward), so links here do not depend on keys at all. The one alchemy-layer verse (1968) makes medicine's promise for the goddess's name. The breath layer is almost absent; only நாதிவாலை (1967) invites it.

literal.reading: Avvai asked whether there is anyone in the world who says the fitting thing so that what is lacking falls into place; the one who says it is the guru.
He who does not know the state in which fullness stands tells lies and recites crores of mantras; he is not the causal guru but an instrumental guru who grabs your goods.

consciousness.reading: The true guru's mark is knowing the standing of fullness (பூரணம்).

social.reading: Against the mantra-reciting guru who takes fees.

literal.reading: Calling themselves all-knowing, full gnanis on this earth, they run about at ease to feed their bellies.

social.reading: Against self-proclaimed gnanis who live by their claim.

literal.reading: Though the primal Vaalai is great, is her elder sister great, or Siva? Though the Vaalai of the channel is great, (not) her lord: Siva is great. The terms are unclear.

breath.reading: நாதிவாலை as the goddess in the channel (நாடி), the power that rises in the body, ranked below Siva.

literal.reading: She gives long life; diabetes and every other disease will not come near; ghosts fly off and sorcery is undone in a moment, if one says the chaste Vaalai's name.

alchemy.reading: A medical claim made for a devotional act: the goddess's name gives long life and keeps diabetes (named first) and all disease away. The verse names no medicine and no practice beyond saying the name; it is recorded as the tradition's claim.

literal.reading: Even in sleep she sits enthroned; at every hour Vaalai stands before you; she thrusts an enemy aside and kicks away even Death when he has come.
She who created as herself everything, from the crores of cosmic eggs and the fourteen worlds to the gods with form, stands in it all like oil within sesame.

consciousness.reading: A pervasion hidden in everything until it is pressed out.

literal.reading: She taught me to make this Vaalai Kummi in Tamil; celebrate the long feet of the heroic Veerapperumal, my guru.
A dedication to a patron, Valaventhiran, who knows the kinds of the six creations, the house and its end, the sutra and the five letters; line 1 has no clear construction.
Dance, all you women, the Tamil that Konganar spoke; sing, all you siddhas; celebrate Vaalai's feet.
Long live the siddhas, Siva, the sages, the gods, the rishis, the devotees, the feet and the guru; long live Bharati, the Vaalai girl.
People go, each in turn, saying they must see the lamp of Annamalai; the lamp of Annamalai is inside you: see it whole and dance the kummi.

consciousness.reading: The light within is to be seen undivided (அகண்டம்).

social.reading: The festival pilgrimage to the Karthigai lamp is turned inward.

literal.reading: They say they must go to have sight of the lingam-lord of Thirukkadaiyur; Thirukkadaiyur and its lord, see them and have sight of them: dance the kummi.

social.reading: The journey to the shrine is set against seeing it where one is.

literal.reading: They say they must see the dance at Chidambaram and all must hurry there; the dance of Chidambaram is inside you: serve it there and dance the kummi.

social.reading: The pilgrimage to Chidambaram is relocated in the body, said outright.

literal.reading: Lifting one foot, he dances the tandava inside you; if you see and serve that holy foot, why go to Chidambaram?

social.reading: The sharpest of the five: the journey is needless.

literal.reading: Saying 'the northern hill', the people of the earth all go; but Venkatesa who lives on the northern hill stands grown tall (presumably within): dance the kummi.

social.reading: The Vaishnava pilgrimage is treated exactly like the Saiva ones: indifference to sect.

links.note: Tirumular says those who have looked over mantra, tantra, yoga and jnana yet do not make them clear and go blind for the sake of food are false gurus; Konganar says the one who knows no fullness, lies and recites crores of mantras is only an instrumental guru who grabs goods. Both make the false guru a man of many mantras and a living, and both test him by what he knows, not by what he recites.

The Kural says none are crueller than those who, unrenounced in heart, live by deceiving as if they had renounced; Konganar's self-proclaimed full gnanis run about to feed their bellies. The shared claim is specific: the claim to renunciation or knowledge used as a living (வஞ்சித்து வாழ்வார்; வயிறு பிழைக்க). The Kural calls it cruelty, the kummi mocks it.

Both give a divine name the power medicine and alchemy claim for themselves: saying the chaste Vaalai's name gives long life and keeps diabetes and every disease away; reciting சிவாயநம is the alchemist's pill (குளிகை) that turns the body's cage to gold. On the alchemy layer the devotional poets take over the physician's and alchemist's promises for the name. Tirumanthiram 2709 is flagged uncertain in its first line, not in the pill.

Tirumular says the form of the human body is Chidambaram and the holy dance; the kummi says the dance of Chidambaram is inside you, so serve it there. Tirumular's identity becomes the kummi's instruction, and the kummi draws the practical conclusion in 1978 that there is no need to travel.

old_links.note: Specific shared marks (mantras recited, teaching as a living), not only a stock attack.
A stock attack on false claimants; the pairing adds only the belly.
Oil in sesame and sugar in milk are different images; the note's 'pressing' does not fit milk.
The lamp against festival-going in both texts; a stock theme made specific by the actual Karthigai lamp.
The Chidambaram dance located in the body in both texts' words.
Pattinathar's empty hall is worldly desire, not the journey to Tillai.
Deceiving by words for gain is in both; graded sound.
Only the name Avvai is shared.
A real conflict over ranking Vaalai and Siva, on the words of both; see findings on stance.
1967's terms are unclear and 1931 only asks the maiden to say.

source_issues: 1975 to 1979 are a separate appended kummi (see the flat marks).
1978 வருத்தண்ட தாண்டவம் not a known dance name.
